newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Workers and students battle riot police in Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Workers and students battle riot police in Seoul.

text.p: South Korean riot police fired volleys of tear gas at about 10,000 students and workers as they tried to march through central Seoul on Saturday, witnesses said.
In one of the biggest clashes this year, radical students threw fire bombs and rocks at police and demanded President Kim Young-sam resign and call off a government crackdown on student dissent.
Witnesses said several students were detained by police and that one student was on fire after being hit by a fire bomb. His condition was not known.
Witnesses said the student was engulfed in flames after police threw a Molotov Cocktail, which had just been thrown at them by students, back at the crowd.
They said the students were part of the radical Hanchongryon student body.

The group has been at the center of a major government crackdown since last August when thousands of rioters were detained after police stormed two teaching blocks occupied by the students on Seoul's Yonsei University campus.

Since the incident, the group has been losing support. A Hanchongryon festival was scheduled this weekend at Seoul's Hanyang University, but police cordoned off the campus to prevent it. Earlier, media reports said hundreds of students from southwestern Korea had forced four trains to stop so they could travel to Seoul.
